'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Internal conflict in Peru]]
**[[San Miguel del Ene attack]]
***Sixteen people are killed in a [[mass shooting]] in a community in [[Vizcatán del Ene District|Vizcatán del Ene]], [[department of Junín]]. A [[dissident]] faction of the [[Shining Path]] is suspected to be behind the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/25/death-toll-of-attack-in-remote-coca-region-of-peru-rises-to-16 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[United States]] sanctions [[Government of Ethiopia|Ethiopian]] and [[Eritrean government]] and [[military]] officials for their involvement in the [[Tigray War]]. These sanctions are intended to push all parties in the war to pursue peace. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/24/us-imposes-ethiopia-sanctions-over-tigray-crisis (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Josep Almudéver Mateu]], the last surviving member of the [[Spanish Civil War]]'s [[International Brigades]], dies in [[France]] at the age of 101. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/last-survivor-spains-international-brigades-dies-101-2021-05-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Afghanistan|Afghan]] truck drivers, faced with roads that have not been repaired by the [[Government ministries of Afghanistan|Ministry of Public Works]], launch a campaign to repair them by themselves by collecting 500 [[Afghan Afghani|Afs]] from their [[trade union]] members to pay for it. Current efforts are focused on the [[Kabul–Kandahar Highway]] and the [[Salang Pass]]. [https://tolonews.com/business-172363 (TOLO News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Mount Nyiragongo eruption]]
**Thirty-two people are confirmed dead following the eruption of [[Mount Nyiragongo]], in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], two days ago. [https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/nation-world/story/2021-05-24/residents-search-for-dead-killed-by-congos-volcano-eruption (The San Diego Union-Tribune)]
*[[2021 Kelana Jaya LRT collision]]
**An underground train collision between the [[KLCC LRT Station]] and [[Kampung Baru LRT Station]] on the [[Kelana Jaya line]] in [[Kuala Lumpur]], [[Malaysia]], injures 213 people, 47 of them seriously. [https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2021/05/692804/213-injured-including-47-seriously-lrt-trains-collide-kelana-jaya-line? (''New Straits Times'')]
*Fourteen people are killed after a truck crashed into homes in [[Guinea-Bissau]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/24/more-than-dozen-killed-in-guinea-bissau-road-accident (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] surpasses 300,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]], becoming the third country to do so after the [[United States]] and [[Brazil]]. India recorded its last 100,000 deaths in less than a month. Experts warn that the real number of deaths could be much higher as many are not officially recorded; some models speculate that about a million people may have actually died. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-57224565 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] opens two mass [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] centres in [[Tokyo]] and [[Osaka]] staffed by [[Japan Self-Defense Forces]] two months before the [[2020 Summer Olympics|delayed Summer Olympics]] as the country aims to vaccinate up to 10,000 people per day in Tokyo and another 5,000 per day in Osaka for the next three months. [https://time.com/6050758/japan-mass-vaccinations-covid-19/ (''Time'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 61 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,309. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-malaysia-record-deaths-icu-more-than-6000-cases-mco-14876944 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Metro Manila]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
*****[[Quezon City]] [[Mayor of Quezon City|Mayor]] [[Joy Belmonte]] receives her first dose of the [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.philstar.com/nation/2021/05/25/2100559/belmonte-gets-first-dose-sinovac (''The Philippine Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taipei]] bans all on-site dining and drinking in response to the continued increase in the number of domestically transmitted COVID-19 cases. All food and beverage vendors are only allowed to serve takeout or deliveries. [https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202105230008 (Focus Taiwan)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delaware]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Delaware]] reports its first case of the Lineage B.1.617 variant that originated in [[India]]. [https://www.wdel.com/news/delaware-sees-1st-case-of-variant-covid-strain-from-india/article_de609c86-bc9e-11eb-b195-af4e4d2f9cf2.html (WDEL-AM)]
***[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] tells Americans not to travel to [[Japan]] due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases there. [https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/japan-olympics-us-covid-travel-advisory/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
***[[Malta]] has vaccinated 70% of its adult population with at least one [[COVID-19 vaccine]] shot, thereby becoming the first country in the [[European Union]] to achieve this [[herd immunity]]-related milestone. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-05-24/malta-has-achieved-herd-immunity-with-covid-shots-says-minister (U.S. News & World Report)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Ryanair Flight 4978]]
**[[Belarus–European Union relations]]
***In response to the grounding of Ryanair Flight 4978 and the subsequent arrest of activist [[Roman Protasevich]], the [[Lithuanian government]] closes its airports to flights from [[Belarus]] and urges its citizens to leave the country. [[Wizz Air]], [[Austrian Airlines]], and [[Air Baltic]] have all rerouted their flights to avoid Belarusian airspace. [https://www.politico.eu/article/european-airlines-swerve-belarusian-airspace-after-ryanair-hijack/ (Politico.eu)]
***The [[European Union]] [[List of air carriers banned in the European Union|bans]] all [[List of airlines of Belarus|Belarusian airlines]] from using its airports and airspace in response to the [[aircraft hijacking|hijacking]], and places sanctions on the officials believed to be involved in the operation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/24/eu-leaders-agree-belarus-sanctions-after-journalists-arrest (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Belarus–United States relations]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] condemns [[Belarus]] for the hijacking and the arrest of Protasevich, and he says that [[Presidency of Joe Biden|his administration]] will "develop appropriate options". [[United States Senate|U.S. Senators]] [[Dick Durbin]] ([[Democratic Party (United  States)|D]]-[[Illinois|IL]]) and [[Marco Rubio]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]-[[Florida|FL]]) urge Biden to ban flights to the country. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-05-25/biden-orders-u-s-to-develop-options-for-belarus-response (Bloomberg.com)] [https://www.businessinsider.com/senators-urge-biden-to-prohibit-us-flights-over-belarus-2021-5 (Business Insider)]
**[[Hamas]] spokesman Fawzi Barhoum rejects the claim by Belarusian authorities that the diversion was caused by a bomb threat from them. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/24/hamas-rejects-belarus-claim-over-plane-bomb-threat (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Colombian protests]], [[Human rights in Colombia]]
**Vice-President and Minister of Foreign Affairs [[Marta Lucía Ramírez]] denies a request by the [[Inter-American Commission on Human Rights]] for on-site visits to investigate growing concerns of police brutality, censorship, and government repression amidst the ongoing [[2021 Colombian protests|civil unrest]]. [https://www.elespectador.com/politica/gobierno-le-dice-no-a-la-visita-de-la-cidh-por-violencia-en-las-protestas/ (El Espectador)]
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**Deposed leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] appears in person in court for the first time since the February coup to face various [[criminal charge|charges]], including "incitement to sedition". During the 30-minute hearing, Aung San Suu Kyi refused to respond on the protests due to alleged lack of information from the outside, wished her people good health and expressed support for her party, which faces dissolution under the [[Military junta|junta]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/myanmars-suu-kyi-appears-in-court-for-first-time-since-coup/a-57638303 (DW)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmars-suu-kyi-appears-court-person-first-time-since-coup-2021-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] begins its trial against [[Janjaweed]] senior commander [[Ali Kushayb]], who is charged with 31 counts of [[war crime]]s. He is the first person to be prosecuted by the Court for personal involvement in the violence committed during the [[War in Darfur|Darfur conflict]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/24/icc-hears-first-war-crimes-case-from-sudans-darfur-conflict (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Law enforcement in India|Police]] raid the [[Delhi]] and [[Gurgaon]] offices of [[Twitter]]'s Indian branch to search for an alleged toolkit used by the oppositional [[Indian National Congress]] to allegedly spread misinformation about [[Indian government response to the COVID-19 pandemic|the government's handling]] of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in India|COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/twitter-india-delhi-police-raid-7328607/ (''Indian Express'')]
*[[Oman]]i police fire [[tear gas]] at protesters in [[Sohar]] as protests break out in the country's major cities. [[Omani people|Omanis]] have been protesting since yesterday over a lack of jobs and worsening economic conditions. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/oman-protests-police-disperse-tear-gas-arrests (''Middle East Eye'')]
*A suspicious package is sent to the home of [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Rand Paul]] ([[Republican Party (United  States)|R]]-[[Kentucky|KY]]). The incident is being investigated by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] and the [[United States Capitol Police]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/suspicious-package-white-powder-sent-sen-rand-paul-s-kentucky-n1268442 (NBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis]]
**Incumbent [[Prime Minister of Samoa|Prime Minister]] [[Tuilaepa Aiono Sailele Malielegaoi]] refuses to concede power to recently elected Prime Minister [[Naomi Mataʻafa]] and a disputed [[government of Samoa|government]] ensues with a [[Faʻatuatua i le Atua Samoa ua Tasi|FAST]] spokesman calling Malielegaoi's move as a "coup". [[New Zealand Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] calls for upholding of democracy and law but rejects any interventionist role whereas the [[Federated States of Micronesia]] is the first country to recognize the legitimacy of Mataʻafa's government. Mataʻafa and FAST MPs remain locked out of parliament on the opening day of the new legislative session. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/443274/samoa-incumbent-leader-rejects-first-female-prime-minister-s-swearing-in-as-treason (RNZ)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/how-samoas-political-crisis-unfolded-2021-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Ecuadorian general election]]
**[[Guillermo Lasso]] is sworn in as the 47th [[President of Ecuador|president]], succeeding [[Lenín Moreno]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/former-banker-guillermo-lasso-becomes-president-in-ecuador/2021/05/24/f8a18db0-bcbe-11eb-922a-c40c9774bc48_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2021 Malian coup d'état]]
**[[President of Mali|Interim President]] [[Bah Ndaw]] and [[Prime Minister of Mali|Prime Minister]] [[Moctar Ouane]] are reported to have been arrested by the [[Malian Armed Forces|military]] and taken to a [[military base]] in [[Kati, Mali|Kati]]. This follows the detection of an increased military presence in [[Bamako]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/military-arrest-malis-president-prime-minister-defence-minister-sources-2021-05-24/ (Reuters)] 
*Dame [[Cindy Kiro]] is announced as the next [[Governor-General of New Zealand]]. [https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/05/prime-minister-jacinda-ardern-announces-dame-cindy-kero-as-next-governor-general.html (Newshub)]
